question.problem:
Consider the change of variables given by the matrix equation

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

and the curve $C,$ defined as

$$
C:\,{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}+2\sqrt{5}{x}_{1}+\sqrt{5}{x}_{2}=\frac{119}{8}.
$$

Given that the change of variables above reduces $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}$ to its canonical (diagonal) form $2{y}_{1}^{2}-3{y}_{2}^{2},$ what type of a quadratic curve is defined by $C?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we note the following:

$$
C:\,{{{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}+2\sqrt{5}{x}_{1}+\sqrt{5}{x}_{2}=\frac{119}{8}
$$

Let's write the given change of variables explicitly: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

 

We know that the given change of variables reduces $Q(x)$ to its canonical form. Therefore, performing the change of variables on $C,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}+2\sqrt{5}{x}_{1}+\sqrt{5}{x}_{2} & =\frac{119}{8} \\ 2{y}_{1}^{2}-3{y}_{2}^{2}+2\sqrt{5}(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2})+\sqrt{5}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2}) & =\frac{119}{8} \\ 2{y}_{1}^{2}-3{y}_{2}^{2}+5{y}_{1} & =\frac{119}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we complete the square for the variable ${y}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1}^{2}-3{y}_{2}^{2}+5{y}_{1} & =\frac{119}{8} \\ 2({y}_{1}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}{y}_{1})-3{y}_{2}^{2} & =\frac{119}{8} \\ 2({y}_{1}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}{y}_{1}+\frac{25}{16}-\frac{25}{16})-3{y}_{2}^{2} & =\frac{119}{8} \\ 2{({y}_{1}+\frac{5}{4})}^{2}-\frac{25}{8}-3{y}_{2}^{2} & =\frac{119}{8} \\ 2{({y}_{1}+\frac{5}{4})}^{2}-3{y}_{2}^{2} & =18\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, performing the change of variables

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{z}_{1}={y}_{1}+\frac{5}{4}, \\ {z}_{2}={y}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{z}_{1}^{2}-3{z}_{2}^{2} & =18 \\ \frac{{z}_{1}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{z}_{2}^{2}}{6} & =1 \\ \frac{{z}_{1}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}-\frac{{z}_{2}^{2}}{(\sqrt{6})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This represents a hyperbola with semiaxes $3$ and $\sqrt{6}.$
